summary: The note presents testimonies from SME owners on how they handled supply chain disruptions after September 1st, 2023. It covers strategies including strong vendor relationships, AI-driven analytics, rethinking just-in-time inventory, localizing supply chains, and personal ties with suppliers. It concludes that flexibility and human connection are central to SME resilience heading into 2024.
one_line: SME owners describe coping with 2023 supply chain disruptions through vendor partnerships, technology, inventory rethinking, localization, and personal relationships.
key_facts: Diana Rodriguez founded 'Bloom & Co.', a boutique retailer in Austin, Texas, and faced delays, soaring costs and quality control issues from overseas textile suppliers in late fall 2023.
Steven O'Neil runs 'O'Neil Adhesives' in Pittsburgh and treats vendors and suppliers as partners rather than just links in a chain.

In November 2023, O'Neil Adhesives' primary resin supplier could not meet demand; open dialogue and transparency about inventory levels and projections led to alternative solutions that avoided stockouts.

May Huang, owner of 'TechTrove', a small electronics wholesaler in San Francisco, invested in an AI-driven supply chain analytics tool around mid-September 2023, valuing its predictive insights on disruptions.

Carlos Alvarez, founder of 'Alvarez Home Essentials', a Miami-based kitchenware producer, was hit by a sudden port strike in October 2023 and reassessed his just-in-time practices to hold enough safety stock without overextending financially.
SMEs with limited storage space or financial bandwidth find stocking up complex, so many explore flexible warehousing and on-demand production.

Jessica Li's 'Green Essence', an organic skincare line, prioritized locally sourced ingredients and was 'somewhat shielded from the biggest shocks' thanks to shorter logistic routes and closer communication with local suppliers.

Marcus Davidson runs 'Davidson Furnishing', a family-owned furniture store in Charlotte, North Carolina, and resolved a failed lumber order through a personal relationship with a supplier he had known for years.
The note says disruptions stemmed from international turmoil, abrupt natural crises, and the lingering aftermath of a global pandemic.
The note concludes that flexibility and human connection are critical as SMEs enter 2024 with an uncertain path ahead.
